description: Modular JavaScript file uploader for web browsers. @uppy/core manages files, state and events; plugins add user interfaces such as the Dashboard, drag and drop, webcam and an image editor, import from remote sources such as Google Drive, Dropbox and URLs through the Companion server, and upload with tus, XHR, Amazon S3 or S3-compatible storage, or Transloadit. Packages integrate Uppy with React, Vue, Svelte and Angular.
rules: Uppy 6 stylesheets are imported through each package's exports map, for example @uppy/core/css/style.min.css and @uppy/dashboard/css/style.min.css. dist/ paths such as @uppy/core/dist/style.min.css are not exported.

@uppy/aws-s3 takes one of three signing options: signRequest (your own signer returns a presigned URL), getCredentials together with s3Endpoint (SigV4 signing in the browser with temporary credentials), or companionEndpoint (Companion signs).

@uppy/aws-s3 sets Companion with companionEndpoint. The older options companionUrl, endpoint, headers and cookiesRule no longer exist. Remote source plugins such as @uppy/dropbox and @uppy/remote-sources still use companionUrl.
@uppy/aws-s3-multipart no longer exists. @uppy/aws-s3 handles single-request and multipart uploads, and by default uses multipart for files larger than 100 MiB (shouldUseMultipart).

@uppy/golden-retriever keeps local file contents in IndexedDB only for files up to 10 MiB each and 300 MiB in total. Larger local files are restored only with its serviceWorker option and service worker set up.

@uppy/drag-drop and @uppy/status-bar are published for Uppy 6 and included in the uppy CDN bundle as DragDrop and StatusBar. In React, Vue and Svelte, the Dropzone component or useDropzone hook takes the place of @uppy/drag-drop.
